## Features

- **`::hot::gzip` and `::hot::zip`: read compressed files without shelling out.** `::hot::gzip` has `encode`, `decode` and `decode-stream`. `::hot::zip` has `entries`, `read-entry`, `read-entry-stream` and `create`, and takes an archive as Bytes or a file path. `read-entry-stream` feeds `iter-csv` and `iter-tsv`, so a large entry can be read a row at a time with flat memory. Reading is checked on real bulk files: SEC Form D, SEC Form ADV and FFIEC Call Report zips.
- **APIs that require compressed responses can be read.** `::hot::http` still doesn't decompress anything, so nothing changes for existing callers. Send `accept-encoding: gzip` and pass the Bytes body to `::hot::gzip/decode`. Checked against the eCFR API, which answers 406 without that header. `http.max-response-bytes` limits the compressed size, and `decode` the decompressed size.
- **Compressed data is treated as untrusted.** `decode` and `read-entry` return an Err once their output passes `compression.max-output-bytes` (64 MiB by default), whatever the input claims about its size. A `max-bytes` option can lower that for one call, never raise it. Corrupt data is an Err, and so is a zip whose headers disagree or that holds two entries of one name. `entries` gives each entry a `safe-path`, which is null when writing the entry out could escape its directory, and `create` refuses such names.
- **`::hot::bytes/to-str` reads Bytes as UTF-8 text.** `Str(bytes)` gives `Bytes([...])`, so there was no way to turn decompressed text, or any other Bytes, into a Str.
- **slack-admin 0.11.0: `::slack::admin::analytics/get-records` returns analytics records, decompressed and parsed.** `get-file` still returns the gzip Bytes. Needs Hot 3.0.3.

## Fixes

- **mcp 1.5.1: `::mcp::tools/call` returns an Err when the server answers with a JSON-RPC error, as its doc says, instead of stopping the run.** `session-request` read the result off the Err, and `tool-result` took it as a `Map`, so on Hot 3.0.2 a refused call or an unknown tool stopped the run before the caller could test `is-err` or read `err-message`. The same holds for `call-tool`, `call-with-input`, `call-tool-with-input`, the `::mcp::client` request helpers and `ping`. On a modern connection, a tool that `tools/list` doesn't return is an Err too.
- **The Kata task worker no longer logs `cni.iptables: rule failed` for a box firewall chain that doesn't exist yet.** It clears a box's `HKT-` chain before creating it, so every box with `network: true` logged four "No chain/target/match by that name" warnings, and eight when its setup retried. It now flushes and deletes the chain only when it exists. A rule that fails to install still warns and fails the box's setup.
- **`hot` processes sharing a package cache can download packages at the same time.** When commands ran in parallel against one cache, such as a CI job checking several projects, downloads from pkg.hot.dev could collide. A process that found another downloading the same version went ahead without waiting, and the temporary directory dropped the last part of the version, so `1.2.2` and `1.2.4` of a package shared one. A command failed with `Failed to extract tarball` or `Failed to clean temp directory`, or, worse, a version was cached holding another version's files and kept them. A process now waits for another's download of the same version, and every extraction has a temporary directory of its own. If a package in your cache shows errors its source doesn't have, delete its version directory under `cache/cdn` (in `HOT_HOME`, the project's `.hot/`, or the user cache directory) to download it again.
- **A package version that doesn't exist on pkg.hot.dev reads as not found.** pkg.hot.dev answers 403 for a missing file, which Hot reported as `HTTP error 403`. It now says the package wasn't found and to check that the version exists, as it already did for 404.
- **File writes on SQLite no longer fail with `database is locked` while another write is in progress.** `::hot::file/write-file` and the other file writes read the account's storage limits before writing, in a transaction that couldn't wait for SQLite's write lock. When another connection was writing, for example `hot run --emitter.type db` recording calls to the same database, the write returned an `Err` with `(code: 5) database is locked` or `(code: 517)` straight away, instead of waiting up to the 30-second busy timeout. File writes now take the write lock first and wait for it. Finishing a task's infrastructure retry had the same problem and is fixed too. PostgreSQL isn't affected.

## Behaviour changes

- **mcp 1.5.1:** code that calls `::mcp::tools/call` or `::mcp::client/ping` and never uses the result no longer stops when the server answers with a JSON-RPC error. Code that reads the result, such as `result.content`, still stops there; test `is-err(result)` to handle the error instead.
